name: error-boundary
purpose: Guards one region of a page. When a component inside the region throws while it renders, sets up or runs a lifecycle hook, the boundary catches the error, reports it through its `error` event, and puts a recoverable message in the region's place: a danger `Alert` that says the section failed and offers **Try again**, which mounts the region again. The rest of the page keeps working. A `fallback` slot replaces the built-in message when the region needs a different shape (a card-sized `EmptyState`, for example).
useWhen: A dashboard card, a side panel, a tab body or any region whose failure should not take the whole page down.
A region that renders data you do not control (a third-party widget, a chart fed by a remote response, a plugin).
Around each route's content inside the app shell, so a failing page leaves the navigation usable (pass the route path as `resetKey`).
When the app reports render errors to a monitoring service: the `error` event carries the error and where it was thrown.
avoidWhen: A request that failed (a fetch, a mutation): that is data state, not a render error. Show it in the region with an `alert` and a Retry, as `platform/states/form-error` and `skills/webkit-ui-states` describe.
A whole page that cannot be shown (missing route, no access, server failure) → use the `platform/states/not-found` block.
A field that failed validation → use `field` with its error message.
Errors thrown in click or submit handlers you can catch yourself: catch them where you call the action and show the outcome with `toast` or `alert`.
related: alert` — the built-in fallback; also what a failed request shows inside a region that rendered fine.
empty-state` — a common custom fallback for a card-sized region.
skeleton` — what the region shows while it loads; the boundary only covers the failed case.
toast` — reports the outcome of an action; never use it for a region that failed to render.
bestPractices: Wrap regions, not the whole app. One boundary per card, panel or route body keeps the blast radius small.
Report every error: listen to `error` and send it to your monitoring service. The boundary stops the error from reaching the app error handler unless `propagate` is set.
Make Retry mean something. Listen to `retry` and reset the state that broke the region (refetch, clear the bad value) before it mounts again; a retry that renders the same bad data fails again.
Pass `resetKey` when the region shows different content for different keys (route path, record id), so moving on from a failed record clears the fallback.
Keep the fallback the size of the region. In a card, use a small `EmptyState`; in a page body, the built-in `Alert` is right.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading of the built-in fallback. Empty uses the locale catalog (`This section failed to load`).

props.name: description
props.doc: Sentence under the heading of the built-in fallback. Empty uses the locale catalog.

props.name: retryLabel
props.doc: Label of the built-in Retry action. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Try again`).

props.name: resetKey
props.doc: When this value changes while the fallback shows, the region is mounted again (pass the route path or the record id).

props.name: propagate
props.doc: When true, the error keeps travelling to the parent boundaries and the app error handler after this boundary handles it.

events.name: error
events.notes: Fires once per failure with `{ error, info }`: what was thrown and Vue's description of where. Report it from here.

events.name: retry
events.notes: Fires when the region is mounted again (Retry, the slot's `retry`, or a `resetKey` change). Reset the broken state here.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The region the boundary guards. Mounted again, from scratch, on every retry.

slots.name: fallback
slots.notes: Replaces the built-in `Alert` while the region is failed. Call `retry` to mount it again.
